The Webster County Health Department (WCHD)/Webster County’s Opioid Settlement Subcommittee received an Opioid Remediation Use request from WCHD’s Operations Specialist and WCHD’s General Assistance Coordinator for the WCHD General Assistance Coordinator and another designated WCHD staff member to provide warm hand-off engagement within Webster County. Two WCHD staff members assisted the Director of The Shining A Light Together (SALT) Heating and Cooling Center (located in the First Baptist Church, Fort Dodge) with individuals having co-occurring opioid/substance abuse disorder and mental health conditions. The two WCHD staff members collaborated with appropriate local agencies and organizations such as local food pantries, public transit, job placement services, and the local community health center for warm hand-off services. Additionally, the two WCHD staff members provided comprehensive wrap-around services to the individuals with co-occurring opioid/substance abuse disorder and mental health conditions, with the completion of housing, Medicaid, and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) applications, for instance. The WCHD’s Community Health Worker (CHW) accessed the National Opioid Settlements portal and documented the received financial allocation amounts. The CHW also researched and studied current and/or future updates on local and statewide prevention, abatement, treatment, and/or recovery for co-occurring opioid use disorder/substance use disorder and mental health conditions. The WCHD’s CHW has maintained a solid rapport with local agencies, organizations, and human service providers through a variety of coalitions. For instance, the CHW is an active member of the North Central Iowa Opioid Task Force. The North Central Iowa Opioid Task Force collaborative efforts supported the prevention, abatement, treatment, and/or recovery resources in Webster County for those with co-occurring opioid/substance use disorder and mental health conditions. The CHW co-led the North Central Iowa Opioid Task Force International Overdose Awareness Day Proclamation Signings with the City of Fort Dodge’s City Council and Webster County Board of Supervisors, and co-led community outreach events that supported annual overdose awarenesses in August. The WCHD/Webster County’s Opioid Settlement Subcommittee received an Opioid Remediation Use request from the Fort Dodge Fire Department (FDFD) for Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD). Matt Price, (then) Interim Fort Dodge Fire Department Chief, stated in the request, “Currently, we are dispatched over the radio and the information gathered by the call-taker is sent to us via our ‘I Am Responding’ app. This process requires the call-taker to gather information up front before paging, burning valuable seconds responders could be on the way to a scene. The Fire Department (FD) will implement CAD to allow us live updates and faster dispatching times. This will increase the information the responders have while on the way to an incident, as well as speed up the time to dispatch after a 911 call is received. Additionally, integrating CAD and the FD’s record management system will provide more uniform data on our incident types and times. So far in 2024, FDFD has responded to 48 incidents that were either overdose related or Narcan was administered. With CAD, our EMS providers will have more information on the way to these incidents, allowing us to more quickly administer Narcan if needed. CAD will also help us respond to these incidents quicker than we are currently can, giving us more time to positively impact the patient’s outcome.” The Subcommittee approved the FDFD request. The WCHD/Webster County’s Opioid Settlement Subcommittee received an Opioid Remediation Use request from Webster County 911-Dispatch (a division of the Webster County Sheriff’s Office (WCSO)) to purchase annual subscriptions, technical services, and project management services for Emergency Medical Dispatch (EMD). The annual subscriptions and services were purchased at the time of the installation, versus purchasing later when costs would be higher. Without the supplemental subscriptions and services, the EMD would be “as is”, which would be a potential determinant to the lives of Webster County. The Subcommittee approved the request. The WCHD’s CHW distributed bilingual (English and Spanish) instructions for DisposeRx (at-home disposable prescription drug deactivation packets) after the distribution of all previously purchased Deterra Drug Deactivation System (at-home disposable prescription drug deactivation pouches).
